blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — recurrent long-QT polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/torsades management
stem: An adult has recurrent polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with a documented prolonged QT interval (torsades de pointes) after an episode has been terminated. Which medication plan is most consistent with the 2025 AHA guideline?

options.A: Consider IV magnesium to treat recurrences associated with the prolonged QT interval while continuing appropriate rhythm and hemodynamic management.
options.B: Use routine IV magnesium for recurrent polymorphic ventricular tachycardia regardless of whether the underlying QT interval is prolonged or normal.
options.C: Prefer IV lidocaine specifically for recurrent long-QT torsades because magnesium is reserved for polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with a normal QT interval.
options.D: Rely on magnesium instead of unsynchronized defibrillation if a subsequent polymorphic ventricular tachycardia episode becomes sustained.

rationale: The 2025 AHA Adult Advanced Life Support guideline states that magnesium may be considered for recurrences of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with a long QT interval (torsades de pointes). It also states that immediate unsynchronized shock is recommended for sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and that routine magnesium is not recommended when the QT interval is normal. Therefore A is the best answer. B overgeneralizes magnesium to normal-QT polymorphic VT, C reverses the guideline distinction between long-QT and normal-QT polymorphic VT, and D incorrectly substitutes magnesium for required immediate unsynchronized shock when polymorphic VT is sustained.
educational_objective: Differentiate long-QT torsades from other polymorphic ventricular tachycardia: magnesium may be considered for recurrent torsades, while sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia requires immediate unsynchronized shock.
source_document_title: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support — 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
source_version_date: 2025 guideline; current AHA guideline page accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Section 16, Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia, Recommendations 1–4: immediate unsynchronized shock is recommended for sustained polymorphic VT; magnesium may be considered for recurrences associated with a long QT interval (torsades de pointes); IV lidocaine, amiodarone, and treatment of myocardial ischemia may be considered for recurrences without prolonged QT; routine magnesium is not recommended when QT is normal.
source_claim_supported: For recurrent long-QT polymorphic VT/torsades, magnesium may be considered; sustained polymorphic VT requires immediate unsynchronized shock, and routine magnesium is not recommended for polymorphic VT with a normal QT interval.
blueprint_locator: Printed p. 38, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate appropriateness and accuracy of medication orders; review pertinent data before medication administration; administer medications safely; evaluate client response to medication; handle and administer high-risk medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four alternatives as parallel rhythm-management plans of comparable length so the correct answer is not uniquely longest.
Clarified that the scenario concerns recurrence after termination, preventing magnesium from being misread as a substitute for immediate defibrillation of sustained polymorphic VT.
Preserved the AHA distinction between long-QT torsades and normal-QT polymorphic VT without introducing an unsupported dose or timing rule.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches AHA Recommendation 2 for recurrent long-QT polymorphic VT. B conflicts with Recommendation 4, C reverses the long-QT versus normal-QT treatment distinction, and D conflicts with Recommendation 1 for sustained polymorphic VT. No second defensible answer or material cueing remains.
